chunks: Hanan, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The people were apostates after the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) except for three. So I said, 'And who are the three?' He said: 'Al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, and Abu Dharr al-Ghaffari, and Salman al-Farsi, may the mercy and blessings of Allah be upon them. Then the people realized after a short while.'

And he said: 'These are the ones upon whom the millstone turned (i.e., the burden of leadership fell upon them), and they refused to pledge allegiance until they brought Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) under compulsion, so he pledged allegiance.'

And Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? And whoever turns back on his heels will not harm Allah at all; and Allah will reward the grateful.
And that is the statement of Allah, the Exalted.

key_terms.دَارَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الرَّحَى: The millstone turned upon them (burden of leadership)

ai.seo_question: Who were the three companions who did not apostatize after the Prophet's death?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the pivotal role of Al-Miqdad, Abu Dharr, and Salman as the steadfast core who resisted the general apostasy (Riddah) following the Prophet's death, while also noting the delayed recognition of others. It connects their resistance to the eventual forced bay'ah of Imam Ali (as), illustrating the transition of authority through the lens of Quranic verse 3:144, which warns against reverting to disbelief after the Messenger's passing. This narrative underscores the Shia view of Ali's legitimacy amidst the broader community's temporary deviation.
